title: Korea Stock Market Today: Nov 11, 2026 - KOSPI Rises 2.60% to 5,375, KOSDAQ Jumps 5.62% Back Above 700 on AI Chip Rebound
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,375.36, up 2.60%, and KOSDAQ closed at 705.10, up 5.62%, as CoreWeave's strong results and AI infrastructure demand hopes outweighed worries over a hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation reading. KOSDAQ regained the 700 level and a buy sidecar was triggered during the session; chip equipment, PCB and test names led.

IndexCloseChange
KOSPI5,375.36+2.60%
KOSDAQ705.10+5.62%

1. Sharp rebound — AI investment hopes return

KOSPI opened at 5,209.71 (-0.56%) and rose as high as 5,377.99 (+2.65%) before closing at 5,375.36. KOSDAQ opened at 668.48 and closed at 705.10, equal to its intraday high.

Korean market coverage said U.S. October CPI came in above expectations, raising rate-hike worries, but CoreWeave's strong results and a positive outlook for AI computing demand restored sentiment. Dip buying after the recent plunge and a rebound in U.S. chip stocks also helped. A buy sidecar was triggered on KOSDAQ during the session.

On KOSPI, foreign investors net bought about 652 billion won (provisional), leading gains in large chip stocks, while institutions net sold about 481 billion won and individuals about 714 billion won. On KOSDAQ, institutions net bought about 314 billion won while foreigners net sold about 134 billion won and individuals about 186 billion won.

2. AI chips and memory

Hopes for HBM and high-performance DRAM demand lifted Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. Samsung Electro-Mechanics gained on FC-BGA package substrates and MLCCs, and SK Square rose as a holding company with a stake in SK hynix.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Nov 11?
KOSPI closed at 5,375.36 (+2.60%) and KOSDAQ at 705.10 (+5.62%). KOSDAQ regained 700 and closed at its intraday high.

Why did Korean stocks rise?
CoreWeave's strong results and AI infrastructure demand hopes, dip buying after the recent plunge, and a rebound in U.S. chip stocks, despite a hotter-than-expected U.S. CPI reading.

Which stocks led?
PCB makers such as TLB and Korea Circuit, chip test names such as Sam C&S and TSE, and equipment makers such as KCTech and Wonik IPS.
